faqs.q: What is the Balanced Bellows Safety Relief Valve, API 526 and what is it used for?
faqs.a: The Balanced Bellows Safety Relief Valve, API 526, relieves into closed headers where back pressure varies. A bellows between disc and bonnet balances the effect of back pressure on the disc, so the set pressure stays true, and it keeps corrosive or fouling fluid away from the spring and guide.

faqs.q: How does the bellows in the balanced bellows safety relief valve work?
faqs.a: The bellows connects the disc to the bonnet and balances back pressure across the disc, so the set pressure does not move as the discharge system pressure changes. It also isolates the spring and guide from the process fluid. The bonnet vent shows a bellows leak, so keep it open.

faqs.q: When is a balanced bellows valve needed instead of a conventional valve?
faqs.a: Use a bellows valve when built-up or superimposed back pressure exceeds about 10 % of set pressure, or varies, or when the fluid would corrode or foul the spring. Dimensions are the same as the conventional valve of the same orifice, so it can replace it in the same envelope.

faqs.q: What is the Thermal Relief Valve, Threaded, 1/2" to 1-1/2" and what is it used for?
faqs.a: The Thermal Relief Valve, Threaded, 1/2" to 1-1/2", is a small relief valve that lets liquid trapped between closed valves expand as it warms, before the pressure damages the pipe or a gasket. A compact, often bonnetless body fits tight spaces, and the inlet can be threaded, union or welded.

faqs.q: Why does trapped liquid need a thermal relief valve?
faqs.a: A blocked-in liquid line heated by the sun or the process can rise thousands of psi, because liquid cannot be compressed. A small thermal relief valve passes a small volume and holds the pressure at the set value.
